summary: More of the daemon's own mail goes to the messages stream instead of the claims graph, where the recipient's host advertises it: capacity-retry wakes, prepare-for-restart notices, plain denial answers, mission-cancelled notices, items routed to their owner, GitHub watch wakes, resource-change notices and workflow-failure alerts. The ones sent from inside a graph transaction go through the message outbox, which delivers them right after the commit (measured p50 11 ms, p99 51 ms) in the order they were queued.

replay.detail: These messages become stream items on members whose recipient host advertises messages_stream_inbox, so the graph stops growing by them. Elsewhere they stay graph claims exactly as before; the outbox falls back to the graph when there is no shard, when the recipient can't take stream mail, or after three refusals.

schema.detail: No schema change: the outbox table and its drain exist since 4c-2. The drain now reads rows in the order they were queued (rowid).

rules.detail: Same routing rule and capability gate as 4c-2b. Ask-ended notices, delegated denial answers, handoff notes and person-authored sends stay on the graph for now, and work wakes follow in a later release.

compatibility.detail: Mixed versions: a sender routes to the stream only when the recipient's host advertises messages_stream_inbox, so an older recipient keeps getting graph claims. An older peer replicates the stream as it already does since 4c-2b.

recovery.detail: Rolling back keeps working: the previous release drains whatever this one left in the outbox, and reads stream mail as before.
